<timestamp>Thursday, Nov 19, 2026, 3:13 PM (UTC-8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
Familiarize yourself with this repo and it's contents
</user_query>
I'll start by mapping the repository structure and the main docs so I know what this project actually contains.

Waypoint is a hackathon demo for international students on F-1, OPT, and H-1B. One Manager bot and four workers (Intake Clerk, Case Clerk, Scout, Messenger) watch case status, mail, and X, then put deadlines on a brief and a phone. A person approves anything that goes to someone else. It is live at https://waypoint-5o4r.onrender.com.

## How it is built

One Node 22 program, no dependencies. `node server.js` serves http://localhost:4173. `node --test` covers the sample day counts, rule packs, and the server end to end.

`server.js` is a small HTTP server. The rest of the backend is in `lib/`:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `config.js` | Paths, signed-in pages, bot names, limits |
| `store.js` | JSON store (`data/store.json`, seeded from `public/data/seed.json`) |
| `accounts.js` | Scrypt passwords, 30-day HttpOnly session cookie, per-account bot keys |
| `api.js` | `/api` routes |
| `bot.js` + `mcp.js` | MCP connector at `/mcp` (13 tools) |
| `persist.js` | Upstash Redis so free Render does not wipe accounts and bot runs |
| `sms.js` | Twilio texts, with daily caps and receipt-number refusal |
| `profile.js`, `csv.js`, `http.js` | Setup checks, optional Google Sheet CSV, request helpers |

The frontend is static HTML under `public/`, with plain JS modules and CSS in `public/css/app/` (later files override earlier ones). Design is black on white, Atkinson Hyperlegible, one green accent, and a pastel per bot.

## Pages

Signed-in: `/login/`, `/setup/`, `/` (Brief), `/activity/`, `/settings/`, `/connect/`. Open: `/portal/` (mock USCIS case status), `/portal/admin/`, `/report/` (bot report form), `/mcp`.

`WAYPOINT_DEMO_ONLY=1` skips sign-in and shows two made-up people, Priya (F-1 OPT) and Wei (H-1B). Add `?p=wei` and `?today=2026-11-18` to rehearse.

## The rules that matter

Deadlines are data, not bot math. `public/js/rules.js` holds rule packs (anchor date, offset, thresholds, source). `public/js/clocks.js` turns a profile plus bot facts into days left and risk. Risk is Act now at 14 days or fewer, Watch at 45, otherwise Clear, with a few rule overrides.

Bots write rows (`runs`, `case_status`, `alerts`, `inbox_facts`, `clock_notes`, `actions`, `notifications`). The server forces emails to `drafted` until the student approves them in the browser. Scout must list its X searches. Texts cannot contain a receipt number, cannot exceed 300 characters, and are capped at 6 per person per day.

Check now, with no real bots connected, simulates Case Clerk against the mock portal and a Manager recount. Both runs are labelled simulated.

The README still has several **TO FILL** lines (interview quotes, timed minutes, bot template links, video, session export) that the team has to complete before submission.

content.text: The docs set a higher bar than the README's open items. I'll check which loops are real in the product and which still stop at sample data.

The site is enough for Best Student Use Case. It is not enough for Best Overall. The gaps that can cost you the track are outside the product: templates, a video of the real bots, student evidence, and a redacted session export. The gap that can cost you Best Overall is that a judge on stage still hits fake data.

## Best Student Use Case

Judges score time saved, a specific student, a workflow that runs, a manager who hands off, evidence you talked to students, and proof Grok Bot helped build it. Hard requirements are five template share links, a video of at most 2 minutes, and public links to the README and a redacted session export. Submit at [form.typeform.com/to/bczKt7rw](https://form.typeform.com/to/bczKt7rw).

The product already covers the workflow they care about: one Manager and four workers, one nightly handoff, deadlines counted in code, and an approval gate the server enforces. The live site, the Brief, and the mock portal are a valid stage for that video.

These items are still empty, and each one is something a judge will look for:

| Missing | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Five template share links | A requirement. Every link has to open. The README still says TO FILL, and the site still says the bots are drawings until you create them in Grok Bot. The PRD says the five bots are already connected. Those two cannot both be true in the submission. |
| 2-minute video of the real loop | A requirement. "It works" means the video, not the site. Show a status change, the Manager waiting on Case Clerk and Scout, a new deadline on the Brief, an approval, then a text or a Gmail draft. |
| Timed "before" and student quotes | The highest-weighted criterion. The minutes table, the one-line impact sentence, and "students we talked to" are all TO FILL. The Open Doors headcount is not a substitute for a measured weekly chore. |
| README sections in your own words | "What we learned", "How Grok Bot helped", and "what the video shows" are still TO FILL. Leave those in and the README fails the every-submission checklist. |
| Redacted Grok Bot session export | A requirement for every track. Names, emails, phones, keys, and tokens removed. |

Do not build more product for this track. Intake Clerk upload, approve-by-text, J-1/O-1/L-1 packs, password reset, and more visual polish will not move the score. The Connect page already has each bot's first message. Turn those into five templates and record the night you already designed.

One check before you record: the PRD still lists four separate clocks (2:00, 2:10, 2:30, 3:00). The track wants the Manager to run the handoffs. The README says that is already true. Confirm the live bots actually wait on the Manager. A video of four independent timers looks like the failure you already wrote up.

## Best Overall

Every team is considered. You can win the track or the grand prize, not both. Finalists have to run whatever a judge picks, live, with no fake data.

That bar is where this demo loses.

- Case status is a mock portal. Sample people are invented. Check now is labelled simulated unless a real Manager webhook is wired. The README says Messenger's calendar and Gmail work live in Grok Bot, and texts do nothing until Twilio is set.
- "No fake data" plus "the judge's pick" means a judge can ignore Priya and the admin page. They can ask for a real receipt, a real school email, or a text to a phone in the room. The happy path through `/portal/admin/` will not survive that.
- The site already looks finished, the user is specific, and the engineering (rule packs, MCP guardrails, approval on the server) is real. Those three criteria you can defend. The live, non-fake run you cannot, yet.

If you want to be in that conversation, add one live path and stop there:

1. Wire Check now to the real Manager so the stage run is not labelled simulated.
2. Put Twilio on the hosted site and send one text to a phone you control. A trial account only reaches verified numbers, so verify that phone before you go on stage.
3. Have Case Clerk or Scout read one real public source the judge can open themselves (the USCIS case-status page, or an official page plus the X post Scout cites). Keep the mock portal as the backup if the government site is down. Say that out loud. Hiding it is worse than naming it.

Setup for a new account is the right answer if a judge offers their own dates. Do not demo a brand-new account unless you have rehearsed it. A new account starts empty, and three of the five bots stay "Not connected" until a real bot reports.

## What to do with the time

Fill the submission, then make one loop real. In order:

1. Publish the five templates and paste the share links into the README.
2. Time one student doing the weekly check, and get two or three short quotes. Put the number in the table and in the one-line impact sentence.
3. Export the Grok Bot session, redact it, and write "How Grok Bot helped" only from what that export shows.
4. Record the 2-minute video on the real bots, one Manager schedule, Priya, then a five-second cut to Wei so the H-1B path is visible.
5. Only after that: Twilio, the Check now webhook, and one real public source.

The demo you have is the right demo for Best Student Use Case once the video shows the bots, not the simulation. It is a prototype for Best Overall until a judge can change a real input and watch a real text or deadline come back.

<timestamp>Thursday, Nov 19, 2026, 3:20 PM (UTC-8)</timestamp>
<user_query>
how can I use grok bot more on this project? I want to ensure I am using it to it's full abilities
</user_query>
The submission is scored on how Grok Bot was used, so I’ll match its actual features against what Waypoint’s bots are already allowed to do.

Waypoint already tells each bot what to do. Grok Bot is only half-used until those instructions are real routines, connectors, a browser, and handoffs on installed bots. The session export is judged on that, so do the work below inside Grok Bot.

## Turn the five prompts into real bots

Paste each first message from `/connect/`, then attach only the abilities that bot needs. A key never goes in the instructions. Each bot asks for it once.

| Bot | Turn on | Leave off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Manager** | The only schedule, 2:00 AM. One routine named "Waypoint check now" whose webhook you paste back into Connect. Handoffs to Case Clerk, Scout, and Messenger. Waypoint MCP. | Its own browser. X, Gmail, Calendar. Any day-counting. |
| **Case Clerk** | Its own computer and browser. Waypoint MCP. | A schedule. It runs only when the Manager asks. |
| **Scout** | X search, and a browser so it can open the official page. Gmail, read only. Waypoint MCP. | A schedule. Reply, forward, delete. |
| **Messenger** | Google Calendar and Gmail drafts. Waypoint MCP, which is what actually sends the text. | A schedule. Sending mail. |
| **Intake Clerk** | Vision. Waypoint MCP, only to call `list_people` for the edit link. | A schedule, and writing the profile itself. |

The Manager's night is the product. It asks Case Clerk and Scout to run, calls `workflow_status` until both have reported, calls `get_brief` for days and risk, saves emails with `draft_email`, then asks Messenger to deliver. Workers with their own 2:10 / 2:30 / 3:00 clocks are the old design. Delete those routines if they exist.

Wire the webhook before you record. Check now should wake the Manager. If it does not, the run on the Brief stays labelled simulated, and the video shows the fallback.

## Use the computer, X, and vision on real inputs

These three are the abilities the prompts mention and a simulated Check now never exercises.

**Case Clerk's browser.** For the demo receipt, it signs into `/portal/` itself and reads the status word for word into `save_case_status`. Then run one receipt on the real USCIS case-status page, https://egov.uscis.gov/. The brief already tells it to do that for a real case. One real lookup in the video is the difference between a bot with a computer and a script hitting your mock.

**Scout's X search plus a browser.** It has to run at least three X searches and pass `x_searches` and `x_posts_read` to `report_run`, or Waypoint rejects the run. A post is not enough. It then opens the official page and passes that link to `save_policy_alert`, with the X link in `x_url`. Use X search, not a web search. If you want monitoring, point an X monitor at the official accounts and have it wake the Manager, which decides whether to start a night. Do not give Scout its own nightly clock.

**Intake Clerk's vision.** The site has no upload. That is fine. In the bot chat, send a photo of a sample I-20 or I-797 with the receipt number covered. It should return each field, the date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, and which Waypoint field it belongs in, and refuse to guess a blurry date. Do that once on camera. It is the fourth worker, and right now the night story skips it.

**Messenger's connectors.** One Google Calendar event per deadline, updated in place. Approved mail becomes a Gmail draft, then `mark_email_delivered` with that draft id. Texts go through `send_text`. If Twilio is not on the host yet, Messenger messages you in the chat and records it with `log_message`. Say that in the video. A silent fallback looks like a broken bot.

## What to do in Grok Bot so the export counts

The track also scores how you built Waypoint with Grok Bot. A thin export of "write me a README" will not. Run these in the session you will export:

1. Have it open the official pages behind the rule rows in `public/js/rules.js` (USCIS, Study in the States, the State Department) and confirm each offset and the date you checked it. Keep the pages that were wrong. That is the research the README promised.
2. Have it call the live connector. "List Waypoint's tools, then `get_brief` for Priya." Then break a rule on purpose: a Scout run with no `x_searches`, and `mark_email_delivered` on a draft you have not approved. The refusals are the guardrails.
3. Hand one code fix to Cursor from that session, such as a failed tool call you just saw, and let it open the PR. The tracks guide calls out Cursor handoff and the GitHub plugin specifically.
4. Ask it for the Manager's webhook routine, paste the URL into Connect, press Check now, and keep the run where the Brief updates from the real bots.

Then export, and delete names, emails, phone numbers, the bot key, the webhook key, and Twilio tokens before you link it. Write "How Grok Bot helped" only from what that export shows.

Talk to students yourself for the minutes and the quotes. A bot summary of forums does not satisfy "you talked to students, measured the before."

## One night to run tonight

Create the five bots, attach the connectors above, and delete every worker schedule. Run the Manager once by hand and watch `workflow_status` go from waiting to reported. Change the mock portal status, press Check now, approve the draft, and confirm a calendar event or a Gmail draft appears. Send Intake one redacted document in a separate chat. That single night is the 2-minute video and the proof you used the computer, the handoffs, X, Gmail, Calendar, vision, and the webhook.

content.text:
You can both change the guardrails in the Waypoint repo. You can change the bots he created only if he shares those same bots with you as a Manager. A template link gives you a separate copy, and edits to your copy do not change his.

## Two different things

**Guardrails live in this repo.** Receipt-number checks, the draft-until-approved rule, Scout having to list its X searches, and "no bot does date math" are in `lib/bot.js` and the server. Either of you can change those in git and deploy. A bot cannot talk its way around them, and his Grok account does not own them.

**Behavior lives on the bot.** The job, the night order, the 2:00 AM schedule, the Check now webhook, and which connectors are attached belong to the Grok Bot account that created it. Telling your own bot "remember this" does not update his.

## How to work on the same bots

Have him share each bot with you, and set your role to **Manager**.

1. In that bot's chat, choose **Share**.
2. Give you access, then set your role to **Manager**. A Collaborator can chat and teach it. A Manager can change settings, routines, and sharing. Only the owner can delete the bot.
3. Open his link. That opens the same bot, not a copy.

Do this for all five. You both then edit one Manager, and the workers it hands off to stay the ones connected to the live site.

Before he shares, he should look through apps, secrets, skills, and files. The Waypoint key should not be written into the bot. The Connect page already tells each bot to ask for the key instead.

## What a template link does

The submission still needs a public template link for every bot. That is a blueprint, not shared editing.

He opens the bot, chooses **Share**, then **Create a copy**, then **Publish**, then **Copy link**. You open it and choose **Add to Grok Bot**. You get your own bot, without his computer, logins, chat history, or the Waypoint key. You connect your copy yourself. Changing yours leaves his, and the one running the demo, as it was.

After he changes the real bot, he uses **Update template** on that same share menu so the public link matches what you will submit. **Delete template** kills the link.

## What to do tonight

He keeps ownership. He shares all five with you as Manager, and he also publishes the five template links for the form. You change server guardrails in the repo. You change how a bot behaves on the shared bot, then he updates the template so the judges' links match.

</user_query>
“Create a copy” means these are personal bots, which only share as templates. I’ll check what has to be true before the Manager role shows up.

That Share menu is the personal-bot one. The Manager role exists only on a Team Bot, and Team Bots require a Team or Enterprise plan with at least one other person on the team. Hackathon access does not include that, so you cannot be added to his bots, and a copy is the only share he can make.

You still split the work like this.

**You edit the guardrails.** They live in this repo, in `lib/bot.js` and the server. His Grok account does not own them. Change them in git and deploy. His bots pick the new rules up on the next call.

**The bot's job lives in his account.** Schedules, routines, connectors, and what it remembers stay on the bots he created. Your copy is a new bot with none of his logins, chat, or the Waypoint key. Editing your copy does nothing to the ones running the demo.

Use `public/js/bot-briefs.js` as the shared script. You change a bot's behavior there and push it. He pastes the new message into the live bot and tells it to remember it and drop the old rules. Then he opens Share and chooses **Update template**, so the public link matches. You install that link when you want to rehearse, and you connect the Waypoint key yourself.

He should stay the only person who creates, schedules, and connects the five bots that the video uses. You own the server rules and the brief text.

content.text:
All six rules are now enforced in `server.js`, on the connector, the report form, and `/api/rows`. A bot cannot skip them by posting straight to the form. All 48 tests pass.

| Rule | What the server does |
| --- | --- |
| Official source | `save_policy_alert` requires an `https` link that is not an X post. A post alone is refused. |
| Texts and logged messages | A receipt number, or anything over 300 characters, is refused on `send_text` and on `log_message`. |
| Quiet hours | `send_text` waits during quiet hours unless a deadline is already Act now. The Settings test button is you, so it still sends. |
| Email | After you approve, the bot can only store a Gmail draft id. `sent: true` is refused. |
| Receipts | Case Clerk can only save a receipt number already on that person's profile. |
| Same door | The report form and `/api/rows` use those same checks. A finished Scout run still has to list its X searches. |

Your partner does not have to change the bots for this to hold. The next time one of them tries to skip a rule, the tool returns the refusal. When he next updates the templates, the Case Clerk and Messenger messages on `/connect/` already match these rules.
